cautions: CORRECTNESS IS THE PRIMARY CONTROL. Every algorithm walkthrough, code/pseudocode example, numeric trace, and complexity claim must be verified — execute the arithmetic and, where feasible, the algorithm itself in Bash (python3/node/etc. may be available; otherwise trace by hand and check) before publishing. A wrong Big-O or an off-by-one in a worked example is a blocking defect.

Big-O / asymptotic complexity claims must be standard and correct. Examples of the expected answers: linear search O(n); binary search O(log n) (requires sorted input); bubble/insertion/selection sort O(n^2); merge sort O(n log n); quicksort average O(n log n), worst O(n^2); hash map / dictionary average-case O(1) lookup, worst-case O(n); stack/queue push/pop O(1); array index access O(1), array search O(n). Distinguish average, worst, and best case, and note Big-O is an upper bound (also mention Big-Theta/Big-Omega where relevant). Attribute the notation to Landau/Bachmann historically and its CS use to Knuth.

Keep examples LANGUAGE-AGNOSTIC where possible (clear pseudocode) or use clearly-labeled Python for concreteness, and note where terminology differs by language — e.g., a Python 'list' is a dynamic array, not a linked list; 'array' means a fixed contiguous block in C/Java; 'dictionary' (Python) = 'map'/'hash map'/'associative array' elsewhere. Do not present one language as the only correct one.

Define data-structure semantics precisely: array (fixed-size, contiguous, O(1) index) vs list (an abstract sequence; may be array-backed or linked); stack = LIFO (push/pop at one end); queue = FIFO (enqueue rear, dequeue front); dictionary/map = key→value with (average) O(1) access via hashing. State the operations each supports and their complexities.

Recursion must include a BASE CASE and progress toward it; always show the base case and warn about infinite recursion / stack overflow. Relate recursion to the call stack (connect to the Stacks topic).
Distinguish TIME complexity from SPACE complexity, and note trade-offs (e.g., a hash map trades space for time). For recursion, note the call-stack space cost.
OOP, abstraction, and decomposition are conceptual — attribute standard definitions, use small correct examples, and do not tie them to a single language.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys yourself from the file. Avoid reusing an identical question-stem template across topics (it triggers cross-topic near-duplicate flags).
